To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PFOS is present in fish from the Western Schelt and the North Sea and that PFOS liver concentration correlates with serum ALT levels and protein liver content in bib.
PFOS concentrations were higher in the Western Schelt than in the Belgian Northsea and that serum ALT but not AST levels correlated positively with liver PFOS concentration in bib.
PFOS pollution in the Western Schelt and the Belgian North sea is confirmed and that PFOS is associated with biochemical effects in bib (T.luscus).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first assessment of PFOS contamination in fish from the Belgian marine and estuarine environment.
the distribution and biochemical effects of PFOS contamination in bib and plaice in the Belgian North and the Dutch Wester Scheldt.
the distribution and the biochemical effects of PFOS in the marine environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results obtained for the two fish species in this study indicate that PFOS is present at low concentrations in both the Western Scheld estuarine and marine environment, but at levels high enough to induce some biochemical effects in the fish liver.

PFOS pollution of the Western Scheldtidem estuary and of the Belgian part of the North Sea is still a concern and that the presence of PFOS in the tissues of the studied fish species is associated with biochemical alterations in the liver of the fish.
PFOS contamination in bib and plaice is a concern in the Western Schelt and the Belgian North sea, but that the observed PFOS concentrations do not cause severe health effects in the fish.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PFOS is a ubiquitous environmental contaminant and a possible risk for the health of the aquatic biota in the area of the Western Scheld estuary and the adjacent North Sea.
PFOS is present in the Western Schelde at levels that are high enough to cause biochemical effects in bib.
PFOS is present in bib and plaice in the Belgian part of the North Sea and in some locations of the Western Scheld estuary and that PFOS may be involved in the induction of liver damage in bib.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PFOS pollution in the Western Schelt and the Belgian part of the North Sea is a real problem.
PFOS pollution in the Western Schelt is still an environmental concern, especially for bib, which is a species of commercial interest.
PFOS is still present in the Western Schelde and the Belgian North Seas and that the Western Schelte is still a hotspot for PFOS contamination.
